drivers: one small product, one release cadence
strong consistency between posts and moderation decisions
low, uniform load; no part needs independent scaling
one data migration from two sources into one database

alternatives.reason: five small features; network calls and distributed data with no scaling or team-independence need
the moderation flow is synchronous request/response; no fan-out or async work in the kept features
no existing system has to stay separate; both sources are merged into one
could add an async notification pipeline later, but no kept feature needs it now

style.reason: Simplest design that meets every driver: one deployable with identity, posts and moderation modules and one database

stack.frontend: Server-rendered HTML pages (Express + EJS templates), progressive enhancement only
stack.sessions: express-session with a PostgreSQL session store (connect-pg-simple)
stack.hosting: a single managed Node host plus managed PostgreSQL (user's choice; not deployed by Feature Mixer)

reasons.backend: D01: A (own code, kept features M01/M05/M07 adapted or improved from it) is Node/Express; B's Python code is not reused, so one runtime
reasons.database: D02: A's schema is PostgreSQL-style (uuid, timestamptz); uuid keys are the compatibility decision
reasons.frontend: D03: neither source's frontend framework is known; five screens need no SPA; server rendering keeps the cookie session simple
reasons.sessions: D04: compatibility decision application:session:session (http-only cookie session, no bearer tokens)
reasons.password_hashing: D05: slow hash required by the security engine; source hashing unknown, so unsupported B hashes force a reset

modules.name: config
modules.responsibility: read every environment variable once and expose typed settings

modules.name: identity
modules.responsibility: accounts, sign-in and sign-out, sessions, roles and the single can(user, action, resource) permission check

modules.name: posts
modules.responsibility: create posts (always pending), read a post with status-based visibility, list published posts

modules.name: moderation
modules.responsibility: moderators list pending posts and publish or reject them through the posts module's API

entities.name: User
entities.notes: B users re-keyed to uuid with legacy_id; same-email accounts merged into A's record; reserved system account for legacy anonymous posts

entities.name: Post
entities.notes: status from A; B rows migrate as published; body limit 10000; author_id not null (legacy anonymous -> system account)

auth.session: server-side session, http-only secure same-site=lax cookie; idle timeout 7 days

role_mapping.B:admin: member (least privilege; listed for the user to promote)

api.auth: public if published; author or moderator otherwise

design_system.icons: none required; an open set (e.g. Lucide, ISC) if added

configuration.SESSION_SECRET: signs the session cookie (secret, required in production)
configuration.NODE_ENV: development | production; production enables secure cookies

slices.name: Core loop: sign in, write a post (pending), read posts with status-based visibility
Moderation queue: publish or reject pending posts

decisions.reason: A is Node/Express and its code may be reused; one runtime

decisions.decision: PostgreSQL 16 with uuid keys; legacy_id for B rows

decisions.reason: five screens; no known source frontend to reuse

decisions.decision: http-only cookie session, no bearer tokens
argon2id password hashing; reset for unsupported B hashes
decisions.reason: security engine s6; source hashing unknown

decisions.decision: Modular monolith with config, identity, posts, moderation modules
Roles member and moderator; B admin -> member
REST JSON under /api, error shape {error: {code, message}}, cursor pagination
Body limit 10000; every new post pending; B posts migrate as published
